title: Al-Infitar: the sky cleaves
hook: what deceived you about your generous Lord, who made you and shaped you (82:6–8)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-Mutaffifin, and the crust that forms over a heart one speck at a time. Your line was hearts rust; hearts shine. Did you polish one habit? Day two hundred ten.

Hold up your hand and look at it. Really look. Twenty-seven small bones, give or take. Tendons that slide like cables. A thumb that can touch every other fingertip, which is why you can hold a pen, a cup, a baby's head. It's so familiar that you only notice it when something goes wrong: a sprain, a cut, a cast. The surah just before Al-Mutaffifin opens with the sky tearing apart, and then, in the middle of that chaos, asks a strangely personal question. It's about you, and the body you're sitting in. Today: Al-Infitar, the sky cleaves.
screen: `LOOK AT YOUR HAND.` → `NOTICED ONLY WHEN IT BREAKS.` → `AL-INFITAR, THE SKY CLEAVES.`

segments.voice: Surah eighty-two begins with four whens. When the sky is cleft apart, infatarat, split like a seam. When the stars are scattered. When the seas are made to burst. When the graves are overturned. Then every soul will know what it sent ahead and what it left behind. And then verse six, in Pickthall's words: "O man! What hath made thee careless concerning thy Lord, the Bountiful, Who created thee, then fashioned, then proportioned thee?" The Lord here is al-Karim, the Generous, the Noble. The question isn't angry. It's almost puzzled. What fooled you? What made you forget the One who was generous enough to make you? And then three verbs, a craftsman's sequence. Created you. Fashioned you, made you complete. And proportioned you, 'adalak, from the same root as 'adl, justice, balance. Two eyes, two ears, two hands, a body in balance, like a scale set level. Then verse eight: in whatever form He willed, He put you together. That's the week, too. It began with Al-Buruj, faith under fire, and al-Wadud, the Loving. Then Al-Inshiqaq, the sky split and the human toiling toward his Lord, and the record in the right hand. Then Al-Mutaffifin, full measure and the rust on hearts. Now the sky cleaves again, and between the splitting sky and the recording angels the surah mentions later, it stops to point at the most ordinary miracle there is: your own proportioned body, sitting right here.
screen: `FOUR WHENS: SKY, STARS, SEAS, GRAVES.` · `AL-KARIM — THE GENEROUS.` · `CREATED, FASHIONED, PROPORTIONED.` · `'ADALAK — BALANCED, LIKE JUSTICE.` · then, large: `SHAPED IN PROPORTION.`

segments.voice: For two minutes, hold one hand in the other. Feel the bones of the fingers, the soft pad of the palm, the pulse at the wrist. Move each finger slowly, one at a time. Notice how much is working without being asked. Then let a word of thanks come, in whatever language you think in. If you pray, you can say alhamdulillah. The bell holds the time.
Al-Infitar. The cleaving, the sky split open, and the name of Surah eighty-two, which asks what made you careless of your generous Lord. Today's word.
Your line: shaped in proportion. Each time you wash your hands today, look at them for one second and remember they were made. Day two hundred ten.

howItsDone: Al-Infitar is among the short surahs Muslims commonly memorize; its question, what made you careless of your generous Lord, is often quoted as a gentle call to gratitude, and its verses on the noble recording angels shape how Muslims think about their deeds.

fork.reveal: What hath made thee careless concerning thy Lord, the Bountiful (82:6): followed by created you, fashioned you, proportioned you.

original.note: Arabic: the Generous, the Noble, a name of God; Pickthall renders it the Bountiful in 82:6.

trapdoor: what you thought: a surah about the sky breaking.
what it means: amid the end of things, a gentle question: what made you forget the generous One who made and balanced you?

what a scholar hears: khalaqa, sawwa, 'adala: create, complete, balance, the same sequence as 87:2; some early scholars remarked that naming God al-Karim in the question almost suggests its answer: His generosity.
